title: Sell Mineral Rights in Graysville, OH
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Graysville, OH
metaDescription: Graysville sits in Monroe County, deep in Ohio's Utica/Point Pleasant core along the Ohio River. See what that means for your mineral value.
heroLead: Graysville sits in Monroe County near the Ohio River, in a stretch of the state where Utica development has run alongside a much older river-oil legacy.
intro: Graysville is a small unincorporated community in Monroe County, one of the counties operators targeted hardest once the Utica/Point Pleasant play proved out along the Ohio River corridor. Monroe County's land was farmed for generations and also carries an older conventional oil history tied to the river valley, so mineral tracts here can have layered production going back well before modern horizontal drilling arrived.

sections.heading: Monroe County's position in the core fairway
paragraphs: Monroe County has seen substantial horizontal drilling activity since the early 2010s, with operators including names like Gulfport Energy and Antero Resources having drilled extensively in the broader area over the life of the play. For a mineral owner near Graysville, that history often means production data exists for the surrounding area even if a specific tract hasn't been drilled directly.

sections.heading: River-valley conventional history layered under Utica leases
paragraphs: Because the Ohio River valley has produced oil since long before the shale era, some Graysville-area tracts carry both an old conventional lease history and a newer Utica-era lease, sometimes involving different operators for each. A deed reserving 'oil and gas' broadly typically covers both, so knowing which wells and which formation apply to your specific interest matters before any valuation conversation.

faqs.question: Is Graysville in an actively producing part of Monroe County?
faqs.answer: Much of Monroe County has seen substantial Utica development, so many tracts near Graysville sit inside producing units, though this varies parcel to parcel.

faqs.question: How do I know if my interest is tied to an old conventional well or a newer Utica well?
faqs.answer: Your lease documents or royalty statements will typically name the specific well and formation. A title search through the Monroe County Recorder can also confirm which leases are recorded against your parcel.

faqs.question: What if my family's minerals have been leased multiple times over the decades?
faqs.answer: That's common in areas with a long production history. What matters for current value is whether an existing lease is still being held by production and what unit it applies to today.

faqs.question: What paperwork should I have ready before a valuation conversation?
faqs.answer: Your deed, any lease or division order, and recent royalty statements if you receive them. Those establish your net mineral acres and decimal interest for a grounded number.
